lines.trans: Max, what are you doing here?
I am just standing and breathing air.
Are you following me again?
You have an important business meeting right now.
Max, tell the truth, are you jealous?
I am not jealous of you at all, Vika.
This is a meeting regarding the sale of the restaurant.
I am calm, go to your meeting.
Please drive my car home.
And you will go in his car?

words.gram: 3rd person masculine singular, accusative; г is said like в

lines.trans: Yes, we will go together to negotiations.

words.gram: particle in the set phrase да ну

lines.trans: It is time for me to go, bye, Max.
Yes, of course, safe travels, Vika.

words.gram: particle in the set phrase да ну

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.text: Стоять на месте, никто не выходит из кухни без разрешения!
examples.trans: Freeze right there, nobody leaves the kitchen without permission!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to breathe'.

examples.text: Лёша, что случилось? Дыши, сынок, дыши!
examples.trans: Lyosha, what happened? Breathe, son, breathe!

meanings.note: the invisible gas substance of atmosphere
Secondary conversational sense ('open air') (outdoor environment) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Успокойся, пойдём на свежий воздух сейчас.
examples.trans: Calm down, let us go outside into fresh air now.

examples.text: Я просто стою и дышу воздухом.
examples.trans: I am just standing and breathing air.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'again'.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

следить.gloss: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ледить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to watch', forming an aspectual pair with 'проследить'.

meanings.en: to look after, to keep an eye on
meanings.note: Secondary conversational sense ('to look after, to keep an eye on') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Keep an eye on the child.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'business', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('businesslike, practical') (about a person) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'meeting', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('see you') (in 'до встречи' = until we meet) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you want me to tell you honestly?

examples.text: Всё честно, Лёха. Взрослые не умеют ждать.
examples.trans: It's all fair, Lyokha. Grown-ups can't wait.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be jealous of'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Are you jealous of my past?
Max, tell the truth, are you jealous?

related.gloss: to be jealous for a while

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.
Secondary conversational sense ('not at all') (совсем не) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'along' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('along, around') (+ dative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('by (phone)') ('по телефону') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'reason', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('about, concerning') ('по поводу' + genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm calling about the shopping centre.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'дажа'). Common feminine noun meaning 'sale' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это встреча по поводу продажи ресторана.
examples.trans: This is a meeting regarding the sale of the restaurant.

examples.text: Ну, как знаешь. Продам его Клавдии Викторовне.
examples.trans: Well, suit yourself. I'll sell it to Klavdia Viktorovna.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'calm' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('good (night)') (спокойной ночи = good night) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это ваша самоуверенность промелькнула. Спокойной ночи!
examples.trans: That was your overconfidence flashing by. Good night!

ехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride

meanings.en: to go, to drive, to ride
meanings.note: by car, bus, train, in one direction, now
Secondary conversational sense ('let's go') ('едем' = we're going / let's go) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Vitalik, we're going to the Santa Fe.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Ну всё, садись скорее в такси, мы едем домой!
examples.trans: All right, get into the taxi quickly, we are going home!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.en: to drive away, move vehicle elsewhere
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'огнать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to drive away', forming an aspectual pair with 'отгонять'.

examples.trans: I will move the van away for now.
The driver moved the car to the garage.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('please') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('you're welcome') (answer to thanks) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('here you are') (handing something over) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

Secondary conversational sense ('machine') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'home'.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ехать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'ехать'.

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

examples.text: Ну всё, поехали быстрее на рынок за свежими продуктами!
examples.trans: All right, let us head off quickly to the market for fresh ingredients!

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'together'.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'говоры'). Common masculine noun meaning 'negotiations, talks' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да, мы поедем вместе на переговоры.
examples.trans: Yes, we will go together to negotiations.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: + infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'for now'.
Secondary conversational sense ('while') (as a conjunction: пока я сплю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('bye, see you') (informal goodbye) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, всем пока, увидимся завтра утром на смене!
examples.trans: All right, guys, bye everyone, see you tomorrow morning on shift!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'of course'.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'happy', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('lucky') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('happy (ending)') (счастливый конец = happy ending) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The film has a happy ending.

examples.text: Ты сейчас один против всех. Счастливого конца не будет.
examples.trans: Right now you're alone against everyone. There won't be a happy ending.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'path', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Here is a movie: A Thorny Path.

examples.text: Давай, счастливого пути и хорошей дороги!
examples.trans: Go ahead, safe travels and have a good road!

examples.text: Ты сам выбрал этот страшный путь.
examples.trans: You chose this terrible path yourself.
